title: [P0] [TPU/PD/Raiden] Client disconnect during chunked prefill kills the prefill engine - aborted request's KV row is released twice
body:
### Checklist

- [ ] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [ ] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [ ] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [ ] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [ ] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

## Summary
A client opens a streaming request with a long prompt (131k tokens) against a 1-prefill + 1-decode pair and closes the connection two seconds later, while the prefill engine is still processing the prompt in chunks. Within a few seconds all eight prefill scheduler ranks exit with the same assertion, the launcher kills the process group, the load balancer goes down with it, and every in-flight and later request fails. 
The cause is a double release of the aborted request's KV row. The chunked-abort path defers the page release because the raiden transfer backend needs its outstanding transfer group to drain first. But the result of the chunk that was already in flight lands one step later and takes the regular aborted-result path, which frees the row immediately. When the deferred path later runs, the row is already gone, and the general release routine treats "release without a row" as legal only for Mamba-style caches. The configuration uses the plain chunk cache (radix cache off), so the assertion fires inside the scheduler loop and the process exits.

**Expected behavior.** A disconnect ends one request and nothing else:

1. The request's KV pages, request slot, metadata buffer and transfer room are released **exactly once**, after the raiden transfer group has drained, so no remote read is still touching the pages when they are reused.
2. Every other request is unaffected: queued requests, requests in flight on the decode side, and the client's next request all proceed normally.
3. Both engines stay healthy and the load balancer stays up; running requests and token usage return to their pre-request values within a bounded time (our test uses 60 s), and a follow-up request succeeds.
5. The event is logged at info level. If the abort bookkeeping fails for any reason, that one request is marked failed and the traceback is logged; the exception never escapes the scheduler loop.

## Code trace

**1. The disconnect becomes an abort for the request that is currently being chunked.** :
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py#L5765-L5768

**2. Next scheduling step: the pending abort is processed and the page release is deferred.** `process_pending_chunked_abort` marks the request aborted, calls `disagg_kv_sender.abort()`, and because the raiden sender declares `group_failure_requires_drain = True` and is not yet drained, it sets `defer_page_release`, drops the cache-side state, and appends the request to `_deferred_chunked_sender_aborts` instead of freeing its pages. It then clears `chunked_req`, so no further chunk is launched:
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py#L3720-L3777
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/raiden/sender.py#L973

**3. The in-flight chunk's result lands and frees the row anyway.**  For an aborted request it calls `_retire_aborted_prefill_result`:
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/prefill.py#L905-L930

That routine checks `req.kv.holds_kv`, which is still true because step 2 deferred the release, and therefore releases the KV row immediately.
It does not consult the sender's drain state and does not know the request is on the deferred list:
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/prefill.py#L1198-L1222

After this, `req.kv.req_pool_idx` is `None` and `holds_kv` is false:
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709/python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py#L969-L970

**4. The deferred path runs and releases the row a second time.** At the top of a later step, `get_next_disagg_prefill_batch_to_run` calls `process_pending_chunked_abort`, which first drains the deferred list. The sender reports drained, and the code calls `release_kv_cache` with no `holds_kv` guard:
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/prefill.py#L672
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py#L3779-L3796

**5. The release routine asserts.** `release_kv_cache` allows a release without a row only for a Mamba-capable cache. `SWAChunkCache` is not one, so it raises:
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709/python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/common.py#L292-L300

```
[TPx] Scheduler hit an exception: Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../sglang/srt/disaggregation/prefill.py", line 757, in event_loop_overlap_disagg_prefill
  File ".../sglang/srt/disaggregation/prefill.py", line 672, in get_next_disagg_prefill_batch_to_run
    self.process_pending_chunked_abort()
  File ".../sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 3734, in process_pending_chunked_abort
    self._drain_deferred_chunked_sender_aborts()
  File ".../sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 3795, in _drain_deferred_chunked_sender_aborts
    release_kv_cache(req, self.tree_cache, is_insert=False)
  File ".../sglang/srt/mem_cache/common.py", line 298, in release_kv_cache
    assert tree_cache.supports_mamba(), (
AssertionError: Only a mamba-capable tree cache allows freeing before alloc
```

**Another concern.** Step 3 frees the pages while the raiden group may still be draining, which is exactly what the deferral in step 2 was meant to prevent. On this run the sender had drained before step 4, so the crash is the only symptom we saw, but a slow drain could let the pages be reused while a remote read is still in progress.


## Fix proposal

1. **Make the deferred list the single owner of the release.**
2. **Guard the drain.** In `_drain_deferred_chunked_sender_aborts`, release only `if req.kv.holds_kv or req.kv.holds_mamba`, matching the guard that `_retire_aborted_prefill_result` and `release_aborted_prefill_waiting_req` already use. 
3. **Contain the blast radius.** A failure in the abort bookkeeping of one request should fail that request, not the scheduler. Wrapping the deferred-abort drain so that an exception marks the request failed and logs the traceback would keep the engine up even if another ordering bug of this kind exists.

A regression test: chunked prefill of a multi-chunk prompt on a `ChunkCache`, abort between chunks with a sender whose `drained()` returns false for one step, and assert that `release_kv_cache` is called exactly once for the request.


### Reproduction

1. Start a gpt-oss-120b pair as in the environment table (prefill with `--disable-radix-cache --chunked-prefill-size 8192`, raiden transfer).
2. Build a prompt of about 131k tokens (any text; needle content is irrelevant).
3. Open a streaming request and close the socket 2 s later. With Python `requests`:
   ```python
   import requests, socket, time
   r = requests.post(LB + "/generate", json={"text": PROMPT, "stream": True,
       "sampling_params": {"temperature": 0, "max_new_tokens": 1024, "ignore_eos": True}}, stream=True)
   time.sleep(2)
   s = r.raw._connection.sock; s.shutdown(socket.SHUT_RDWR); s.close(); r.close()
   ```
   or: `python scripts/abort_test.py --url $LB --prompt-file prompts/gpt-oss/131072.jsonl --phase prefill --abort-after 2 --repeat 1`.
4. Wait 15 s. `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' $PREFILL/health`.
5. `grep -A12 'Scheduler hit an exception' <prefill log> | head -20`.



### Environment

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| sglang-torchtpu | `main` @ 09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709 (2026-10-07), sglang 0.5.13.dev7249 |
| TPU stack | torch-tpu 0.1.1+release.2026.9.22.20260927223741, libtpu 0.0.47, tpu-sync-torch 0.0.1.dev20261002213151, torch 2.11.0+cpu, transformers 5.8.1 |
| Hardware | Two TPU v7x hosts (4 chips / 8 TensorCores each). Host a: prefill engine. Host b: decode engine. TP 8, EP 8 on each |
| Model | `openai/gpt-oss-120b` (MXFP4 weights), KV cache fp8_e4m3, page size 64 |
| Prefill flags that matter | `--disaggregation-mode prefill --disaggregation-transfer-backend raiden --disable-radix-cache --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --context-length 140288` (overlap scheduling on; tree cache is `SWAChunkCache`) |
